# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Customers unable to submit forms (POST /checkout → 403)
**Description:** During 17:32–17:52 UTC, legitimate POST /checkout form submissions from a normal browser (Chrome 141, client 198.51.100.80) returned HTTP 403. Cause: CommonRuleSet SizeRestrictions_BODY blocked bodies exceeding the ~8 KB inspection limit — ~1,200 blocks. Recovered after 17:52.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:32:00Z - 2026-10-06T17:52:00Z

### Automated client receiving 403s (GET /catalog, /home → 403)
**Description:** During 18:05–18:25 UTC, an automated client (198.51.100.70, AWS range) with no User-Agent header received HTTP 403 on read-only GET /catalog and /home. Cause: CommonRuleSet NoUserAgent_HEADER — ~599 blocks. Recovered after 18:25.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T18:05:00Z - 2026-10-06T18:25:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: CommonRuleSet is the sole source of all WAF blocks
**Description:** 100% of the ~1,799 blocked requests during the incident are attributable to AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (priority 3, Block action). Its per-rule BlockedRequests values are byte-for-byte identical to the WebACL-level Rule=ALL series; every other rule (AntiDDoS, AmazonIpReputationList, KnownBadInputs, SQLi) produced zero blocks, and the rate-based rule is Count-only. Blocking occurred in two distinct bursts — 17:32–17:52 UTC (~60/min) and 18:05–18:25 UTC (~30/min) — with a quiet gap between, suggesting two separate false-positive patterns matching the two reported symptoms (form submissions vs automated clients). Baseline (16:00–17:30) had zero blocks.
**Cascades to:** symptom-form-403, symptom-automated-403

### Root Cause: CommonRuleSet applied with default Block and no overrides/scope-down
**Description:** The fundamental cause: web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 applies AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet at priority 3 with default Block and no RuleActionOverrides or scope-down. In this window two sub-rules each matched a stream of legitimate traffic — SizeRestrictions_BODY (oversized /checkout POSTs) and NoUserAgent_HEADER (UA-less automated GETs) — producing all ~1,799 403s. CloudTrail shows no config change, so the trigger was traffic matching pre-existing rules (Inputs-category cause). Tuning these two sub-rules stops the symptoms recurring without weakening other protections.
**Cascades to:** symptom-form-403, symptom-automated-403

## Other Gaps

### [RESOLVED] Verbatim NoUserAgent_HEADER block record retrieved via Athena
**Description:** CLOSED. Earlier, no verbatim WAF log sample of a NoUserAgent_HEADER block could be retrieved: those records live in the large 'flood' log objects (Artillery load-test volume) that exceeded the tooling's 200k-token parse limit, S3 Select was disallowed on the bucket (MethodNotAllowed), byte-range reads broke gzip, and GetSampledRequests was unavailable (3-hour retention; incident ~9 days old). This gap is now closed: the verbatim NoUserAgent_HEADER BLOCK record was successfully retrieved using the Athena `waf_logs` table (CROSS JOIN UNNEST(rulegrouplist), filtering action='BLOCK'), which filters server-side and bypasses the oversized flood-file limit — confirming clientIp 203.0.113.47 (US) POST /api/cart and /api/checkout with no User-Agent header.
